Comments: On 9/16/2022 at 10:43, I arrived on location to conduct a follow up inspection on a referral from the Water Quality inspector. The wellhead was corroded and covered in rust. Bubbling was noticed between the surface casing and the production casing. (Picture 1) This bubbling was on going throughout this inspection and was going at the max rate of severe and constant. It was also observed that there was brown staining on the ground around the wellhead and some very small gravel. There was a faint odor what might be best described as diesel fuel. The brown staining did not appear to be due to the corrosion on the wellhead. The production equipment was on location. There was a substance covering one side of the Kimray (picture 4) and a spill or a leak from a valve between the line heater and the seperator (picture 6). The production tank did not show any leaks around the base of the tank during this inspection. The last APR for this location was submitted for the 2020 year. The last MIA submitted to the Department was for the 2015 inspection year. The violations from previous inspections have been continued.

Comments: On May 7, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection at the Sanns Frank well site in response to violations issued in IR 4165270.The ESCGP (ESG076322011-00) for this site was issued on 8/27/2021 and was set to expire on 8/26/2026, but was terminated on 11/6/2024 (IRs 3862784 and 3863032).There are 8 total wells on-site at this time. The 1H, 2H, 3H, and 7H appear to be completed and equipped for production at this time. The 4H, 5H, 6H, and 8H wells have all reportedly begun stimulation activities. During today's inspection, the following was observed:- Stimulation operations are currently ongoing on site at time of inspection. According Completions Supervisor Lou Offerman, the operator is currently stimulating the 6H well.- Act 9 sign is present and complies with 78a55 fabrication requirements. Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan are present on site and include the required components (Photos 1, 25).- Access road appears to be in good condition, no E and S issues were observed along the access road at this time. - CFS has been installed above the existing 12" culvert at STA 8+00 of the access road (Photo 2). The CFS appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time. - The area below the MRC Rain Garden #2's rip rap outlet (Photos 7-12) appears to be seeded and mulched at this time with erosion control blanked installed over top. This area appears to be stabilized at this time and no further E and S issues on or off LOD are observed at this time.- CFS at the stream crossing of UNT to Mingo Creek (Photos 13-16) appears to have been replaced and appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time.- Sedimentation is observed along the CFS at this area. Additional gravel was reportedly added by the operator, however it is only noticeable near the CFS on the west side of the crossing at this time. - Areas of third party disturbance below MRC Rain Garden #3 and the rock apron (Photos 17-20) do not appear to be seeded and mulched, however these areas also do not exhibit any active E and S issues at this time, including any channelized flow paths to UNT to Mingo Creek. - Additional third party disturbances along the access road (Photos 21-23) also do not appear to be seeded and mulched, except for the disturbance in Photo 23. - Disturbance along the access road closer to the well site (Photo 24) appears to be seeded and mulched at this time.The Department recommends the operator seed and mulch the third party disturbances to prevent potential E and S issues from developing.The Department requests a written response from the operator indicating a timeline for the paving of the access road where it crosses UNT to Mingo Creek that was mentioned in the NOV response (IR 4192276). Violations issued in IR 4165270 for PCSM BMPs not maintained by operator are being corrected at this time.Violations issued in IR 4165270 are being continued for the sedimentation observed along the access road.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, corrosion, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. All valves were open and the well is currently equipped for production. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. NO methane was detected in the slam bar holes utilizing a MSA ALTAIR 5X meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023. No casing string pressures were observed at the time of inspection due to no pressure gauges in place and no operator provided well tender available. This well was labeled with an incorrect well API#, this issue was brought to the attention of the operator and promptly fixed. Further inspections of this well may be warranted to determine the root cause of the complaint.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/21/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 989365
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/21/2023
Comments: On 3/21/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident - response to an accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. On 3/18/2023 Chesapeake reported that 10 gallons of produced water sprayed out of a damaged pipe on a GPU unit, the water impacting the unprotected pad surface. Creston Environmental identified the extent of the impacted area and excavation was scheduled for 3/20/2023. It was 39 degrees and clear when I arrived on location.When I first arrived at the site, I met Chesapeake's Pat Adams who described activities with the event. Pat showed me a pipe nipple on the 1HC GPU that had been replaced. He showed me the excavated area that is in the northeast corner of the site. The excavated hole had not been backfilled at the time of the inspection. The excavated area is roughly 12' x 40' with various depths up to 2', running along the edge of the perimeter berm. The GPU had been moved from the affected area and had not been returned back to its original position. Pat said that a truck driver first witnessed the spill. Upon discovery, all ten wells were shut in. Pat had just put the 9 unaffected wells back into production before my arrival. The 1HC was still shut in until the GPU is reinstalled. The excavated material remains on site and has been piled on a plastic sheet on the southeast corner of the pad. I field tested some small water puddles in the bottom of the excavated area with results being as high as 4.18 mS conductance. Using a Hanna Gro-line soil probe, I probed the side of the excavated area with one reading being 1.03 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance of the water and soil with Chesapeake's Eric Hottenstein. Eric said he would have someone probe the excavated area to determine if further excavation was necessary. Eric also reported that it was their practice not to fill in the excavated area until they had gotten confirmation samples back. Danielle Schaad met me on location before I left and we discussed the elevated conductance areas. She said that they would excavate some more of the area as determined by the results of field tests.There were nine wells staged for production and one offline at the time of the inspection. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. Comments: On April 15th, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill incident reported to the Department for the Gospel Church Unit 10H Well Site in Plum Borough, Allegheny County. The Department reached out to Marc Jacobs of Penneco for additional information on the spill. Per Mr. Jacobs, the well tender discovered the spill on 4/15/2022. The spill occurred at a broken valve on one of the production tanks due to freeze/thaw. They estimate approximately 1 barrel of crude oil has been released and contained within the earthen dike. Cleanup crews have been called to the site. At this time, released oil is being absorbed with pads and peat soil until remediation efforts can continue on Monday. On Monday, 3rd party consultant (Woodard Curran) will be onsite to evaluate release. The affected production tanks will be removed and release area will be remediated. At time of inspection, several Penneco representatives were onsite finishing preliminary clean up efforts. Per Penneco representative, the release was discovered around 10am on 4/15/2022 by the well tender. The spill was estimated to occur sometime between 4/12/2022 (the last visit to the well site) and 4/15/2022. Penneco rep estimated release to be about 1 barrel at the production tank. A vacuum truck was onsite to remove surface crude oil from the release site. Rep stated that on 4/18/2022, two of the three tanks are to be removed and release area to be excavated. Release site was isolated within the dike around the production tanks. Absorbent pads and peat laid within the release area. The broken valve and pipe laid within the dike. There also appeared to be a release at the well head. Per Penneco Rep, there was a release of approximately 5 gallons from around the pump jack. Follow up inspection to be conducted upon completion of remediation efforts. The Department recommends Operator remediate impacted area IAW spill policy for releases greater than 42 gallons. The Department requests the following: disposal records/ manifests for removal of all impacted materials once available, quantity released at the production tank valve and at the well head, how quantity was determined, method of remediation, timeline of when the remediation will be completed, when the release around the wellhead occurred, why the release around the well head occurred and what was released at the well head. Based on today's observations, violations are being issued.

Comments: Inspection 1 of 2:On February 18, 2025, the DEP conducted a two part Incident Inspection of the Herminie Well Site (ESCGP-3 issued: 12/12/2024, expires: 12/11/2028), located in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 2/14/2025 by CNX representative Mr. Andrew. The spill report states that as CNX dug into the well pad to install secondary containment and production equipment, water and diesel fuel filled the hole. Refer to Part 2 of this inspection for details on soil samples that were collected at the time of this inspection.At the time of this inspection, the Herminie Well Site has reportedly been acquired from Apex Energy by CNX.At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 sign was at the access road entrance and inside the onsite mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, all of which had Apex Energy's name and information on it. The access road which was graveled appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. Once on the well pad, the DEP was accompanied by CNX representatives, Mr. Andrew, Chad Eisenman, and Carrie Crumpton. Mr. Andrew informed the DEP that at the time of this inspection, operations were in the drill out phase, fracking was completed last week and flowback would be starting next week. Mr. Andrew showed the DEP the spot where the first hole was dug, the DEP observed a partially frozen red substance mixed with what appeared to be frozen water that was giving off a strong petroleum based odor. Mr. Andrew stated that several test holes were then dug until CNX found a point in each direction where the fluid was no longer observed, this determined the extent of the impacted area, which appeared to approximately 60ft x 90ft with 8 total holes marked with cones to identify them as contaminated.At the time of this inspection, Penn E and R was on site with plans to excavate the area and place all contaminated material into a roll off dumpster on site. CNX could not provide the DEP with an approximated quantity of this release, but theorized that it may be over 42 gallons and plans to follow Act 2 protocol for this release. Once contaminated material is excavated, CNX hopes to have a more definitive quantity for the release. At the time of this inspection, the DEP inquired whether CNX believed any waters of the Commonwealth were impacted and Mr. Eisenman explained that the pad has catch drains all around the perimeter which discharge into an infiltration basin on the back right corner of the well site. Mr. Eisenman also stated that all catch drains and discharge points are routinely plugged during all Alteration Operations and that they were closed prior to CNX discovering the substance in these holes. The DEP also inquired when CNX hypothesizes the spill occurred, Mr. Andrew and Mr. Eisenman both stated that they believe the spill occurred when Apex Energy was operating the well pad (According to Department records, Apex Energy has not reported a spill at the Herminie well site regarding diesel fluid in this area of the well pad).Due to the spill reportedly occurring prior to CNX acquiring this well site, at the time of this inspection, the DEP collected soil samples to determine what the substance may be and to determine if this substance reached the infiltration basin prior to the drains being plugged. Refer to Part 2 for details on the collected soil samples.CNX is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations, and how CNX quantified the amount spilled.CNX will need to follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and CNX is requested to assess the impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the release.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for a release on the well pad.

At the time of this inspection, the DEP inquired whether CNX believed any waters of the Commonwealth were impacted and Mr. Eisenman explained that the pad has catch drains all around the perimeter which discharge into an infiltration basin on the back right corner of the well site. Mr. Eisenman also stated that all catch drains and discharge points are routinely plugged during all Alteration Operations and that they were closed prior to CNX discovering the substance in these holes. The DEP also inquired when CNX hypothesizes the spill occurred, Mr. Andrew and Mr. Eisenman both stated that they believe the spill occurred when Apex Energy was operating the well pad (According to Department records, Apex Energy has not reported a spill at the Herminie well site regarding diesel fluid in this area of the well pad).Due to the spill reportedly occurring prior to CNX acquiring this well site, at the time of this inspection, the DEP collected soil samples to determine what the substance may be and to determine if this substance reached the infiltration basin prior to the drains being plugged. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations, and how CNX quantified the amount spilled.CNX will need to follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and CNX is requested to assess the impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the release.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for a release on the well pad.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: This administrative inspection report is in response to the receipt of analytical results for sample number 4406-019 collected on 7/18/2024 at 11:57 AM as part of inspection report #3798130 at the Tract 726 D Pad. Elevated levels of metals and chlorides in the sample analysis indicate a release of a pollutional substance.Sample 4406-019 indicated elevated concentrations of the following parameters: Aluminum - 1.6 mg/L; Barium - 11.0 mg/L; Strontium- 1.44 mg/L; Specific Conductivity- >3,230 micro-ohms/cm; Total Chloride- 600.6 mg/L (photos 1 and 2). PGE submitted an NOV response letter to the Department on August 2, 2024 which stated the following actions were taken regarding the Department's 7/18/2024 inspection: "PGE had a vac truck take up the puddled fluid immediately. A 50 X 15 X > 3 deep area of soil was then dug up and loaded into a lined roll off for sampling and disposal. PGE asserts that it was not in violation of any state or federal regulation nor was PGE acting contrary to the permit issued under the authority of the Department. It cannot be established that the puddled fluid was caused solely by any activity conducted by PGE rather than a combination of mat washing and heavy rainfall."In follow-up inspection #3801042, the Department verified that impacted material was being scraped from the site and placed into a lined rolloff container for sampling. As the volume of pollutional material released to the pad surface has not been measured or quantified, the Department recommends PGE pursue Act 2 remediation response in accordance with 78a.66. Violations noted.

Inspection Date: 2019-02-06
Comments: The Department, Frank Hoehle, DEP O&G WQS and I arrived at the site at 11:39 to conduct a follow up inspection in reference to a production fluid spill that occurred at the site on 1-6-19. The weather conditions are cloudy skies, breezy, with rainfall approaching, and a temperature of 35 degrees Fahrenheit. For additional details pertaining to the production fluid spill, refer to the Department's 1-6-19, 1-9-19, and 1-17-19 inspection reports, Inspection ID#'s 2831500, 2832214, 2832221. We met with Murray Kush, site company man, completions consultant of Repsol, and Dave Coxhead, Site Safety Man, of REM Security. Deep Well Services Rig # 2 is in the process of drilling out hydraulic fracturing plugs. Mr. Kush informed the Department the following. "The rig is drilling out frac plugs on the 3H well. A total of 22 plugs will be drilled out. We are the 20th plug. The 1H is done. Frac plugs will be drilled out on the 7H next. The working tanks and gas buster tanks near the pad entrance contain fluid from the 3H plug drill outs. Brine was used on the 1H well to drill out the plugs. Fresh water is used to drill out the plugs on the 3H well. Trucks are removing water from 1H plug drill outs, out of the offloading station near the production equipment. Containment is the same since the frac. We added containment under the rig. Gel is used to drill out plug parts." In addition to conducting a follow-up inspection at the site, the Department conducted a review of sample results for a water sample collected at the site on 1-9-19. The PADEP Bureau of Laboratories in Harrisburg, PA forwarded the results to the Department on 2-6-19. On 1-9-19, the Department collected a groundwater sample from the swale at the base of the Caprio Pad where the water exhibited elevated levels conductivity on 1-8-18. The Department identified this water sample as Caprio Pad SW-1. Upon review of the Department's groundwater sample results, it was noted that the sample results had elevated concentrations of barium, lithium, manganese, strontium, aluminum, chloride, and iron. Barium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential Medium Specific Concentration (MSC) for groundwater of 2,000 micrograms per liter (ug/l) with a concentration of 50,600 ug/l. Lithium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 83 ug/l for Residential, Used Aquifers and for Non-residential, Used Aquifers of 230 ug/l with a concentration of 1,270 ug/l. Manganese was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 300 ug/l with a concentration of 8,000 ug/l. Strontium was detected above the Act 2, Residential and Non-residential MSC for groundwater of 4,000 ug/l with a concentration of 38,900 ug/l. Aluminum was detected above the Act 2, Secondary Maximum Contaminant Level (SMCL) of 200 ug/l with a concentration of 41,400 ug/l. Chloride was detected above the Act 2, SMCL of 250,000 ug/l with a concentration of 946,000 ug/l. Iron was detected above the Act 2, SMCL of 300 ug/l with a concentration of 34,400 ug/l. Bromide was detected at a concentration of 7,307.28 ug/l. Calcium was detected at a concentration of 252,000 ug/l. Sodium was detected at a concentration of 389,000 ug/l. Specific See the attached sample results. During the inspection, I utilized a Hanna Groline Soil Test HI 98331 meter, and an Oakton PCTS 50 meter to record specific conductance (conductivity) in water in the sump in the infiltration basin at the toe of fill slope, and in water and damp soil west and slightly up-gradient of the sump, where groundwater seeped to the fill slope. Conductivity readings were in the range of (170-240) microsiemens/cm in the sump, and (700-800) microsiemens/cm in water west of the sump, and (150-200) microsiemens/cm in wet soil west of the sump. See photos. The Department left the site at 12:43.

properties.content:

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.

Permit API: 035-21329
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/13/2022
Comments: On December 13, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline, John Ciccone, and Amber Boyd conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. At the time of inspection, the recently stimulated wells were in flow back. This inspection is to follow up with the multiple spills at this site. About half of the containment from the recent stimulation process has been removed. With the removal of some of the containment STL was able to excavate the area of elevated conductivity off the east end of the containment found on October 24, 2022. The area of excavation was about 90 ft. x 45 ft. and about 8 to 12 inches deep. The second area of elevated conductivity has been excavated to the containment. Containment remains in this area for the flow back process. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources was onsite and said STL Resources plans to continue the investigation of the extent of this spill area once the containment has been removed. The top layer of soil has been removed in this area adjacent to the containment in about a 10 ft. x 10 ft. area. Soil conductivity could not be screened in either of the excavated areas due to the ground being frozen.The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of thewell pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being hauled off site or pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in the northwest stormwater vault. In the southwest stormwater vault, the conductivity of the water was 1,939 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.3 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 23.7 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 71.9 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 133.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32 uS/cm. Seep 3 was not able to be screened with the conductivity meter due to the lack of water at the seep. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 90.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.6 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, 3445592, and 3467217.

Unconventional: No

Comments: Cement plugs were set in well bore on 04/21/2021. An inspection was conducted on 04/21, as well as on 04/28/2021, when the top hole section of well bore was being filled with pea gravel. Fluid in wellbore was static during both inspections. A vent monument had been set in the top of the surface casing, but had not yet been cemented in place. During todays inspection, a significant amount of bubbling was observed in the fluid inside of the surface casing. An Altair 5x gas meter was used to check the vent and the bubbling fluid for stray has. Methane reading was 27% volume in the vent, and 10% volume at the top of fluid. Gas is likely entering the well bore in the 1500'-1150' range. Pea gravel and casing seat plug will have to be drilled out in order to assess necessary remedial procedures. I will inspect the well one week from today to determine if the venting gas is residual. Violations cannot be closed until the vertical flow of gas to surface has been eliminated. Violation Code: 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID: 8164676
Permit API: 125-22304
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/06/2023
Comments: On November 6 2023, the Department conducted an inspection of the Cole 1 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the production tank leaking what appeared to be production fluid. At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled and equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, it appeared the production tank had previously been leaking at a valve near the bottom of the tank, but did not appear to be actively leaking. Distressed vegetation was observed in an approximate 3 foot radius around the tank. Directly below the valve, there appeared to be an excess amount of fluid along with a thick oil based matter. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.15 mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the soil in the area of the spill. The readings were elevated in comparison to the background reading with readings of 0.25mS, 0.45mS, 0.39mS, and 0.46mS. Elevated readings were detected in about a 3 foot radius around the production tank. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted KPI Representative Joel Greco to inform him of the release. Mr. Greco indicated that they had already replaced the faulty valve, and estimated the spill was roughly 15 barrels of production fluids and impacted the ground roughly 8 inches in depth. He stated remediation was scheduled to begin on 11/8/2023. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity and type of fluid released (including the oil based matter) and how this was determined, as well as how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid (and/or other fluids) resulting in a release to the ground, as well as failure to report a release.

Comments: Site inspection conducted to review residual waste processing activity. Meeting on site today with STL Company Man Tim Fields. The intent of the authorization for onsite drill cuttings processing is to remove the solid fraction from the liquid (drilling muds and fluids) so that drilling fluid can be reused concurrently for further drilling. For more information, refer to the Form A application regarding drill cuttings processing (EFACTS authorization #1400373).During this inspection, conductivity screenings were taken within rig secondary containment, production fluid containment, and GPU containment. Fluid within containment for the 1009H GPU is observed with conductivity reading of 3.8mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming all secondary containment features associated with production equipment. All containment structures are in good repair and are functioning as designed.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM - Headwaters 146 Well Pad located in Ulysses Twp, Tioga Co on 11/30/22 @1300 hours in response to a release of between 5 and 42 gallons of completions fluid into secondary containment and onto the pad surface. The weather was 45 degrees, rain, winds W @15mph. Terra Tokarz, JKLM Env Field Coordinator was present onsite. JKLM was in the process of dewatering a transfer line into the frack tanks when a cam lock on the hose failed. Mrs. Tokarz stated the majority of the fluid was captured by the tank secondary containment, but a revised estimate of 10 gallons was released to the pad surface in a spray. The impacted area was approximately 15' x 30" off the back side of the frack tanks. Approximately 1" of pad material was removed from the impacted area and placed in a dump truck on secondary containment until a waste container could be procured. The area was screened for field conductivity and found to be <1.0mS/cm. Elevated fluid was still located in the secondary containment. Mrs. Tokarz stated the vacuum truck onsite is routinely removing the fluid from the secondary containment. JKLM stated they had screened the pad E and S controls and no elevated conductivity was found. Due to conditions onsite observed during this inspection, it appears the spill has been adequately remediated.Violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against the 2HU (API#105-21923) well:25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)SWMA 301CSL 402(b)I departed the site at 1430

Violation ID: 8253897
Permit API: 115-23194
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Springville Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/23/2025
Comments: On 10/23/25 Casey Baldwin, O and G WQS and I were at the Coterra Energy Lauer D. Well Site in Springville Twp., Susquehanna County from 1057 to 1301 hours in response to a well control incident that occurred around 8 AM on 10/22/25. An unknown amount of natural gas and production fluid released out of the 12H well as a result of the well control incident. The weather conditions are overcast skies and chilly with light to moderate west winds, occasional gusts, and temperatures around 50 degrees Fahrenheit. The intent of the inspection is to determine if an impact occurred to the ground surface outside of the Limit of Disturbance (LOD) due to the well control incident.Shortly after arrival we met with Mike Oakley, CHMM, and Environmental Health and Safety Specialist of Coterra and the Coterra contractor Resource Environmental. The Department, Coterra, and Resource walked around the entire perimeter of the well pad and tank pad near the site LOD in a clockwise direction to determine if an impact occurred. We started just west and off the intersection of the site access road and Garrison Road near the Site ID signage. The Department utilized a Hanna Groline HI 98331 Soil Test Meter and an Oakton PCTS 5 meter to perform field conductivity screening of wet soil and small pools of fluid on the surface of the ground off the well pad. Resource utilized a Hanna HI 98192 meter. Conductivity readings do not indicate the release of production fluid has extended off the well pad. See photos for additional details.If you have any questions, do not hesitate to contact me @ 570-346-5533 or jsassi@pa.gov.
